m.ctx.tuttiReadme:
# Tutti

Tutti creates this folder in every project; it holds what the agents need to know. It is versioned with git, so the whole team shares the same thing. Subfolders only appear when you add something from the Tutti tab.

- `specs/`: one folder per feature or bug, with `requirements.md` (or `bugfix.md`), `design.md` and `tasks.md` (`- [ ]` checkboxes).
- `docs/`: documentation by category (Diátaxis): `tutorials`, `how-to`, `reference` and `explanation`.
- `steering/`: guides for the agents. `contexto.md` is the project context. An `inclusion: always | fileMatch | manual | auto` header says when each one is handed over.
- `hooks/`: one `.json` per hook, in Kiro's format. They do not run until you allow them in the project.
- `skills/`: reusable skills (one folder per skill, with its `SKILL.md`).

sf.title: Create a spec
sf.subtitle: A spec turns an idea into requirements, a design and a task list, as in Kiro. It is saved in .tutti/specs.
sf.type: What are you going to do?
sf.describePh: Let the customer gather products in a cart and pay for them in one step.
sf.describeBugPh: What fails, how to reproduce it, what you expected and which code must not be touched.
sf.reqFirstHint: You define what the system must do (stories and EARS criteria) and then how to build it. Good with clear user stories.
sf.designFirstHint: You define the architecture first and then the requirements that follow from it. Good when there are technical constraints.
sf.name: Name
sf.templateHint: The files are created with their structure and you fill them in.
sf.agentHint: The open agent fills in each phase and waits for your approval before moving on. It does not write code.
sf.noAgent: Open an agent so it can write it.
sf.needDescription: For the agent to write it, describe what you want.
stf.title: Create a steering file
stf.subtitle: Markdown guides that agents receive in every session, so you do not repeat your conventions. They are saved in .tutti/steering.
stf.name: Name
stf.h.always: Handed over whole in every session. This is the default.
stf.h.fileMatch: Handed over whole when files matching the pattern have changes; otherwise it is only listed with its path.
stf.h.manual: Not copied: it is listed with its path so the agent reads it when you mention it.
stf.h.auto: Not copied: it is listed with its description so the agent reads it when it applies.
stf.descriptionPh: REST API design patterns. Use it when creating or modifying endpoints.
stf.refs: Inside the text you can link real files with #[[file:path]], #[[file:path:12-28]] or #[[folder:path]]: they are replaced with their content when handed over.
stf.baseBody: Creates product.md (the product), tech.md (the technology) and structure.md (the structure): all three are always handed over.
stf.baseAgent: Ask the open agent to fill them in by exploring the project
stf.baseNoAgent: Open an agent so it can fill them in.

## What it is

## How to run and test it

## Conventions
m.ctx.prompt:
Write the context of this project so that other coding agents read it before working on it.
Write it in Markdown, in English, at most 25 lines, with these sections: "## What it is", "## Structure", "## How to run and test it", "## Conventions".
Use only what appears below; if something cannot be known, leave it out instead of inventing it. Reply ONLY with the Markdown, with no explanations or code blocks wrapping it. Do not use tools or read files: everything needed is here.
